Resolves #19256

`.claude/settings.template.json` allows five more git verbs without a prompt: `git checkout -- *`, `git restore *`, `git rebase *`, `git push --force-with-lease origin *` and `git push --force origin *`. The `agent/*`-scoped force-push row goes, since no seat uses that prefix any more. Every `dev` / `main` deny row stays as it is, and deny outranks allow, so the force-push rows reach feature branches only.

The operator approved both allowances on 2026-09-26: "approved on my end", and "force pushes into feature branches are fine too => we squash merge every PR to dev". After this lands, the operator updates each seat's real `.claude/settings.json` from the template; this PR does not touch them.

Evidence: L1 (the file parses; the rows are checked by name) → L1 required for AC-1 / AC-2.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `JSON.parse` of the template succeeds; all five rows are present in `permissions.allow`; no `origin agent/*` row remains; `permissions.deny` is unchanged (11 rows, no diff lines) |
| AC-2 | This body quotes both approvals and names the per-seat follow-up |

## Deltas from ticket
None.

## Test Evidence
The diff is 6 lines in and 2 out, all in `permissions.allow`.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Documented search — I evaluated the rule set instead of reading the claim, and here is the whole result.** Eight command shapes, each tested against allow ∪ deny:

| command | allow | deny | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git push --force origin dev` | ✓ | ✓ | **refused** (deny wins) |
| `git push --force origin main` | ✓ | ✓ | **refused** |
| `git push --force-with-lease origin main` | ✓ | ✓ | **refused** — `--force*` matches `--force-with-lease` |
| `git push --force origin HEAD:main` | ✓ | ✓ | **refused** — via `git push* *:*`, the only row that catches a refspec |
| `git push --force origin dev2` | ✓ | ✓ | **refused** — `dev*` is a prefix glob, so it is conservative in the right direction |
| `git push --force origin feature/x` | ✓ | — | **allowed** — exactly the operator's approval, feature branches only |
| `git push -f origin main` | — | — | **default prompt** — nothing allows or denies it |
| `git push origin main` | — | ✓ | denied (pre-existing) |

The seventh row is the one worth naming, and it is **not** a finding. `git push -f origin main` falls to the prompt because the two `-f` deny rows are shaped `git push* -f * origin main*` — with a wildcard between `-f` and `origin` — so they match `git push --no-verify -f origin main` but not the minimal spelling. That is fail-*safe*: nothing in the allow list covers `-f`, so the minimal spelling prompts rather than proceeding. Worth knowing only so nobody "helpfully" adds a `Bash(git push -f *)` allow row later and silently opens the minimal spelling.

**Challenge (non-blocking): the body's safety argument is stated one level above where the guarantee lives.** "Deny outranks allow, so the force-push rows reach feature branches only" is true, but the reason it is true is that the deny rows glob the subcommand position and cover the refspec form — neither of which the sentence mentions. If a future edit narrows `git push* --force* origin main*` to `git push --force origin main*`, the sentence stays true-sounding and the guarantee quietly stops holding for `--no-verify --force`. One clause in the body naming the deny rows' shape would make the next reader check the shape rather than the principle.

**The red, named exactly.** `baseline / PR body` fails with `First missing: ## Post-Merge Validation` — the body has an `## AC Evidence` section and the approvals quoted, but no `## Post-Merge Validation` heading opening a line. One section, and the per-seat follow-up is already written in the prose, so it needs a heading rather than new content. The check also wants the invisible `Depth Floor` / `Required Actions` / `Strategic-Fit Decision` anchors and the seven metric tags; `/tmp/check-anchors.mjs` reproduces all four checks locally in milliseconds if you want them verified before the next push.
